column1: # The dynamic-linking scenario.
#   FEED_SCENARIO=tools/smoke/dyn.tsv sh tools/smoke/feed.sh <log> <seconds> <qemu command…>
# Driven by `just test-dynlink-x86`, which builds the loader and the two C
# artifacts and injects all of them into the image (`DYNLINK_BINS`).
# One step per line, as `tools/smoke/scenario.tsv` documents: the command, a tab,
# and the whole line its output must produce.
# `/bin/dynhello` is a non-PIE `ET_EXEC` with `PT_INTERP /libexec/ld.so` and
# `DT_NEEDED` for two shared objects. Its single line holds one value per
# mechanism the loader has to get right:
#   dynlink-ok     libdyn's `JUMP_SLOT` — the main's PLT call, resolved by name
#   dynlink-data   libdyn's `RELATIVE` — some of the object's own data, reached
#                  through a pointer the loader must rebase; unfixed it is a wild
#                  address, not a wrong number
#   dynlink-2-ok   libdyn2's `JUMP_SLOT` — the second object, which only resolves
#                  if the loader gave it a base of its own
# None of those strings is in the executable: `just test-dynlink-x86` fails the
# gate if it is, which is what makes this line evidence about the loader rather
# than about the program. One line, not three, because the harness matches whole
# lines anywhere in the log — a second expected line would be satisfied by the
# first run's output and prove nothing.
/bin/dynhello
